title: Remediation plan for sustained KV cache memory regression causing capacity pressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the 2025-02-13 capacity event we observed a sustained, platform-wide increase in resident memory footprint attributed to the KV/prefix cache. Impacted Dedicated clusters experienced degraded throughput and transient OOM pressure; several autoscaling policies were triggered and two worker nodes were reprovisioned. This ticket contains the triage notes, root-cause findings, and concrete remediation and prevention work.
details:
Timeline: 2025-02-13 01:20 UTC - Alerts for gradual memory growth on kv-cache shards. 2025-02-13 02:10 UTC - Ops rolled back runtime change (GH#3421) as immediate mitigation. 2025-02-14 - Heap diff and heap-profiling showed retained prefix entries grew without expected eviction. 2025-02-15 - Repro harness validated regression under long-tail prefix distributions.
Root cause (short): A change to the eviction heuristics intended to reduce oscillation (introduced in GH#3421) inadvertently increased hysteresis for prefix eviction when shard-local pinned prefixes exist. For workloads with many short-lived prefixes and irregular token lengths, the heuristic prevented timely eviction of cold KV entries. Over time the retained set grew across shards, causing memory pressure and degraded throughput. The change also disabled a defensive path that proactively trimmed cached entries during GC pauses.
Why this wasn't caught by tests: Existing integration tests used uniform prefix distributions and synthetic load that didn't model the heavy-tailed prefix churn patterns from customer workloads. The regression only appears with many small prefixes across concurrent sessions and long-running processes (seen in Dedicated).
immediate_mitigation:
- Rolled back GH#3421 in production to restore previous eviction thresholds.
- Temporarily lowered per-shard cache hard limit (config override) to trigger earlier trimming for affected clusters.
- Enabled an emergency autoscale policy for Dedicated pools to add headroom while the fix is implemented.
- Alert rule added: rate of retained prefix growth per shard > 5% over 30m now alerts on-call.
long_term_fixes:
- Rework eviction heuristic to account for 'prefix churn' metric instead of single-step hysteresis; add unit tests for churn scenarios. (owner: Jonas Meyer, due: 2025-03-07)
- Reintroduce and harden the defensive GC-trimming path but gate behind performance tests. (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2025-03-14)
- Add synthetic load tests that model heavy-tailed prefix distributions and session concurrency; integrate into preflight CI. (owner: Diego Ramirez, due: 2025-03-21)
- Backport fix to runtime-1.18 and prepare a patch release for on-prem customers. (owner: Release Eng, due: 2025-03-10)
- Add dashboard panels and a long-term SLO for retained-key growth rate by pool. (owner: Observability, due: 2025-03-14)
